column1: # THE DECLARED CLAIMS OF THE PIPELINE — one row per cornerstone x boundary, WRITTEN BEFORE THE
# ARTIFACT IS BUILT.
# ==WHY A SECOND TABLE, WHEN `DECLARED.tsv` ALREADY EXISTS==
# `DECLARED.tsv` records WHAT AN ARTIFACT IS (`REAL`/`IDENT`/`TRIVIAL`/`LAW-JUSTIFIED`/
# `SINGLE-SIDE`/`BUDGET`) and is REGENERATED FROM THE OBSERVED STATE (`--declare`), which makes it a
# regression guard: it catches a cell whose kind changed.  It cannot catch a cell that was never
# meant to be `TRIVIAL` in the first place, because it learns the expectation from the emission.
# 's independent-construction requirement is the reason that matters: the honest baseline was ~8 REAL cells,
# not 19.  Eleven of the twelve REAL `.egg` cells compare one program against
# `Reflect(tnodeOf(resT))` -- the executor's own output."  A table derived from what was emitted
# cannot report that, because the emission is exactly what is in question.  So THIS table is the
# CLAIM, written first, by hand, and 2A.1 is the task that fills it in; the audit then measures the
# artifacts against it (`scripts/audit_pipeline_markers.py`) and a cell that came out weaker than
# its declaration is a failure rather than a new declaration.
# ==THE SCHEMA==
# The column list is `Certified.ClaimsColumns` (src/main/scala/Certified.scala), declared in code so
# the emitter and the two readers cannot disagree about the order.  Tab-separated, `#` comments.
#   cornerstone    aunt | datalog-sn | gol | puzzle15 | temperature | nqueens | puzzle3-full
#                  (CornerstoneTypes.scala is the authoritative list -- seven, not six)
#   boundary       space | zipper | graph, i.e. which of the three stages this cell crosses:
#                    space   SPACE/TERM vs its optimisation (`SC.reduce`)
#                    zipper  the Scala `transpileZ` observation vs SPACE/TERM
#                    graph   `optimize(transpile(...))` vs SPACE
#   form           instance | agnostic.  `instance` is one ground input; `agnostic` quantifies the
#                  inputs and is the strictly stronger claim.  BOTH are declared per cell, because
#                  "the agnostic leg is TRIVIAL" is a fact about the emitter that a reader needs.
#   claim          one line, in words, of the equivalence this cell asserts.  It is prose on purpose:
#                  the machine-readable part is the other columns, and this is the part a reader
#                  checks the other columns AGAINST.
#   trusts         the `; TRUSTS:` list this cell is PERMITTED to carry, in `Certified.Trust`'s
#                  vocabulary: `T<n>` (docs/TRUSTED.md), `O<n><letter?>` (a registry's OPEN row),
#                  `law:<name>` (proofs/laws/REGISTRY.tsv), `outside:<construct>`, or `-` for
#                  nothing.  The emitted artifact's own `; TRUSTS:` header must be a SUBSET of this;
#                  a cell that trusts something its declaration does not permit is a failure.
#   artifact       repo-relative path of the emitted obligation.
#   expected-kind  REAL | LAW-JUSTIFIED | IDENT | TRIVIAL -- the `DECLARED.tsv` vocabulary.
#                  `SINGLE-SIDE` and `BUDGET` are deliberately ABSENT from what may be DECLARED:
#                  2A.2 deletes the single-side emission at its source and 2A.5 requires a BUDGET
#                  cell to be closed by decomposition rather than by budget, so declaring either
#                  would be declaring an outcome the plan forbids.  An artifact that comes out as one
#                  of them therefore fails against every possible declaration, which is the intent.
# ==THE DECLARED MATRIX (2A.1), written 2026-09-04 BEFORE the emitter of 2A.2–2A.6 was built==
# Seven cornerstones × three boundaries × two forms = 42 cells, one artifact each.  The kinds and the
# permitted trusts below are what the emitter is REQUIRED to reach; `scripts/audit_pipeline_markers.py
# --accept` fails a cell that comes out weaker (BUDGET, SINGLE-SIDE, BOUNDED-UNROLLING are never
# acceptable), that trusts something not listed here, or that has no row here.  A stronger outcome
# than declared (a REAL prover run where LAW-JUSTIFIED was declared, or sides identical where a law
# chain was declared) is accepted and reported.
#   space    the program vs `SC.reduce(program)`, discharged by THE TRACE (`SC.reduceTraced`, 2A.3):
#            every step a checked instance of a certified optimiser law, composed end to end.  The
#            instance form (`.smt2`) records the chain and the per-step executor differential on this
#            input; the agnostic form (`.egg`) re-derives each step in egglog under formal.egg's rules,
#            falling back to the step's ∀-certificate where the ladder does not converge.  Three stones
#            are TRIVIAL: `SC.reduce` leaves them syntactically unchanged, and that is stated, not
#            proved.  `law:*` permits any law of proofs/laws/REGISTRY.tsv; the artifact names the ones
#            actually used.
#   zipper   `transpileZ(program)` vs the program, an INSTANCE of the universal refinement theorem
#            (proofs/lean/Zippy/Zipper.lean#Zippy.Zip.refinement, registry law `zipper-refinement`):
#            the emitter abstracts every materialising subterm (Iteration, Fixpoint, Call, Fold,
#            Range, TailsIntersection, grounded) to an opaque hole, transpiles the remaining SHELL with
#            every source opaque, and checks that the shell read back from the cursor is alpha-equal
#            to the shell it came from.  The theorem does the semantics; the cell records the shell
#            size, the boundary constructors, and (instance form) the executor differential.  `O6a` is
#            permitted where the program has a `Call` hole, `T5` where it has a `Range`.
#   graph    `untranspile(optimize(transpile(P)))` vs `P`, the pre-existing data-agnostic leg: the
#            differing pairs are law-justified (`SmtDiff.partition`) and any residual pair is a small
#            prover obligation on the pair, never on the whole program.  Both forms use the SYMBOLIC
#            program (binders kept), so no cell compares materialised literals; the instance form adds
#            the executor differential `runGraphT == eval` on this input.
# Kinds declared from the 2026-09-04 baseline measurement (`SC.reduce` is the identity on datalog-sn,
# gol and temperature; `optimize` changes only puzzle15 and puzzle3-full), so a declaration below that
# the emitter contradicts is either a measurement error to be re-derived here — with the change
# recorded in build.log — or an emitter defect.  RE-DERIVED 2026-09-04: gol's graph cells trust T5 —
# the game-of-life rules contain a `Range`, which the first declaration missed (build.log).
